title: Tanzanian Beef and Potato Stew
community: The most complete everyday Tanzanian stew
author: Mama Salima
desc: Mchuzi wa Nyama na Viazi — Tanzanian beef and potato stew. Tender beef and potatoes simmered together in a rich spiced tomato sauce until both are falling-soft and the sauce is thick and glossy. The complete, filling, everyday Tanzanian meal in one pot.
longDesc: Beef and potato stew is the one-pot meal that Tanzania's families rely on — the potatoes bulk out the beef, thicken the sauce, and create a complete, satisfying meal that stretches further than beef alone. It is eaten with ugali, chapati, or rice.
steps: Cook onions until golden. Add garlic, ginger, spices.
Return beef. Add water. Simmer 35 minutes.
Add potatoes. Simmer 20—25 more minutes until potatoes are tender.
The potatoes naturally thicken the sauce.
chefTips: Add potatoes after the beef is halfway cooked — they cook much faster.
The potatoes thicken the sauce naturally — no flour needed.
Do not stir too much once potatoes are added — they break apart.
commonMistakes: Adding potatoes at the start — they disintegrate.
Stirring too much with potatoes in.
cookingScience: Potato starch leaches into the sauce during cooking, naturally thickening it without the need for flour or cornstarch. This starch thickening also creates a slightly glossy, silky consistency.
sustainabilityTips: Potatoes are grown across Tanzania's highlands — locally sourced.
healthBenefits: Complete meal — protein from beef, carbohydrate from potato.
Potatoes add potassium and vitamin C.
culturalNote: Beef and potato stew is Tanzania's most practical everyday dish — the meal that feeds a family on a modest budget without compromising on flavour or satisfaction.
